name: detail-progress
description:
Five hundred computers across five inventory pages, each costing its own detail call. That second loop is where a real tenant spends its run: one request per page plus one per device, so a 10,000-device Jamf is 10,000 serial round trips with nothing on the console between them -- a slow run and a hung one look identical.

The assertion is the periodic progress line. PROGRESS_EVERY is 500, so exactly one line must appear, at the 500th detail call, and the run summary that follows must agree with it. A line per device would be 10,000 lines on that same tenant, which is why the interval exists at all.

The detail route is a single prefix match with 500 scripted responses consumed in order, because the walk requests them in page order; each carries its own udid, which is what becomes the asset id.

The mobile walk is served one empty page so it ends immediately -- this scenario is about the computer detail loop.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy: the id is a bare Jamf udid with no tenant scope.

REQUEST COUNT. jamf.star refreshes its OAuth token every MAX_REQUESTS (100) requests, so the count is API calls PLUS one token POST per 100 of them, not a single token fetch: 500 detail + 6 inventory + 1 mobile = 507 API calls, plus 6 token POSTs = 513. The old expectation of 508 assumed one token for the whole run.

log_contains: jamf: fetched details for 500 computers so far
jamf: read 500 computer and 0 mobile inventory item(s), reported 500 assets
